Priya — thanks. I've skimmed the resume. A few quick notes for the panel (high level anchors so we score consistently):

Role scope we want to validate:
- Ownership: end-to-end ownership of production inference stacks (deploy, rollback, observability)
- Performance: meaningful work on latency/throughput tradeoffs, batching, KV cache strategies
- Reliability: incident response experience for model-serving regression and hotpaths
- Mentorship & hiring: ability to lead a small infra pod and raise operating standards

Leveling anchors (Sr vs Staff):
- Sr: owns a single service boundary or cross-team feature, can design robust APIs and performance plans, handles major incidents with guidance.
- Staff: sets cross-service architecture, drives cost-performance initiatives, measurable impact across teams.

Interview logistics and focus areas:
- System design (45m): design an inference gateway for multi-model routing with latency SLOs
- Troubleshooting scenario (25m): real incident postmortem + live debugging questions
- Behavioral / leadership (20m): mentorship, tradeoffs, influencing without authority
- Deep dive (30m): code/path-level question on KV caching / batching decisions (bring a notebook of a prior implementation)

Scoring guidance: use the eval-anchor-template (attached) — 1–4 per dimension plus a pass/fail safety/security gate.

Vivek — can you add any probe questions you want for the deep dive and trouble-shooting? I'll block the above times if Marissa confirms panelers.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate Jordan Lee — scheduling and quick scope/context

Thanks Grace — adding specifics below (I copied them into the eval-anchor-template and attached a PDF):

Primary probe areas (examples):
- Throughput/latency tradeoffs: "Design a batching layer for requests with variable prompt lengths — how do you avoid head-of-line blocking?" Expected Sr-level answer covers dynamic batch windows, timeout heuristics, and opportunistic padding; Staff also reasons about kernel selection and cross-model batching policy.
- KV cache correctness and efficiency: "You have stale KV entries across replicas — how do you detect and recover while minimizing tail latency?" Look for metrics-based detection and incremental repair strategies.
- Rollout safety: "A model rollout increases hallucinations; you need a fast rollback plan that preserves cache warmness. What do you do?" Gate: must mention automated canary metrics, fallback model variant, and cache invalidation plan.
- Incident postmortem: ask for a prior incident write-up — evaluate causal analysis and blameless remediation.

Behavioral anchors:
- Candidate must show examples of mentoring, hiring, or process improvements (we award extra points for concrete numbers: reduced p95 by X, cut cost/Y%).

Scoring notes:
- Use 1–4 per axis; any '1' on safety/security or 'fail' in the canary/rollback plan should be a blocker.
- For Staff consideration, look for cross-team influence and measurable cost/perf impact beyond a single team.

Attachments referenced: eval-anchor-template.pdf (filled), sample-probe-list.txt

I'll be on the panel if timing works — prefer Thu 1–4 PT.

— Vivek
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
